“זה כל‑כך קשה,” האיש שישב מולי אמר. “אנחנו נשואים כבר כמעט חמישים שנה, אבל לא ציפיתי לשום דבר כזה.”

\n

“מה קורה?” שאלתי את אל, בהזדהות.

\n

“זו ליסה,” הוא אמר. “אתה יודע שהזיכרון שלה מתחיל להיתפס פחות טוב כבר קצת זמן. אז הלכנו לנוירולוג, כמו שאמרת לנו, והם הוציאו לא מעט בדיקות וסוג של סריקת מוח. ואז הם אמרו לה שיש לה דמנציה.”

\n

“חשבתי שזה מה שקורה,” עניתי.

\n

“אני יודע שאמרת את זה,” אמר אל. “טוב, יש רגעים שהיא לא מכירה אותי. היא מסתכלת עליי כמו במבט ריק, כאילו תוהה איזה זר משוגע נכנס לה לבית.”

\n

“זה בטח קשה,” אמרתי.

\n

“הדבר היחיד שמחזיר אותה לעצמה הוא לצאת החוצה ולקרוא לה בסלולרי. אני אומר לה לצאת למוסך, שיש לי משהו להראות לה. איכשהו כשאני עושה את זה, זה מחזיר אותה להווה ומזכיר לה מי אני – לפחות לזמן מה.”

\n

עברנו לדבר על נושאים אחרים, אך יכולתי לראות שלב אל נשבר. אשתו מזה 48 שנה נראתה מבחוץ אותו הדבר, ובכל זאת היא אדם שונה לחלוטין.

\n

ארצה לבחון כמה מהאתגרים שבלטפל בדמנציה.

\n

דמנציה בתנ\"ך

\n

קהלת 12:1-7 מצייר תמונה יחסית מדוכדכת של תהליך ההזדקנות. “הִזְכַּר עָתָה בּוֹרְאֶךָ בְּיְמֵי־נְעוּרֶיךָ, עַד־כִּי לֹא יָבוֹאוּ יָמִים רָעִים וְלֹא תִמָּלֶה שָׁנִים; כְּשֶׁתֹּאמַר אֶת־יָגֵעַ בָּם, לֹא אֶשְׂמַח־בָּם. בִּהְיוֹת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ אוֹ הָאוֹר אוֹ הַיָּרֵחַ אוֹ הַכּוֹכָבִים לֹא יִכָּהוּ; וְלֹא שׁוּבוּ הֶעָנָן אַחַר הַגֶּשֶׁם. בְּיוֹם שֶׁיִּרְעֲדוּ שׁוֹמְרֵי־הַבַּיִת, וְנָטוּ הַגְּבַרִים; וְתַכֵּל הָרַחֲצָה כִּי מָעָטִים, וְהַנֹּצְנִים שֶׁמִּן־הַחַלּוֹנוֹת יִכָּהוּ; וְהָיוּ הַדְּלָתִים סְגֻרוֹת בָּרְחֹבוֹת, כְּשֶׁתִּתְרַעֵם קוֹל הַטְּחִינָה, וְיָקוּם בְּקוֹל־הַצִּפּוֹר, וְכָל־בְּנוֹת הַשִּׁיר יִדְּמוּ. גַּם כְּשֶׁיִּפָּחְדוּ מִמְּרוֹמִים, וְיִהְיוּ יְרָאוֹת בָּדֶרֶךְ; וְתִנְבְּטֶה הַשָּׁקֵד, וְשָׁכֵר הַחֲגָבִית יִהְיֶה לְעֹמֶס, וְתִכָּלֵא הַתְּאַוָּה; כִּי־אִישׁ יֵלֵךְ אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ הָאָרוֹךְ, וְהָלוֹכִים בַּשְּׁוָא יַהֲלֹכוּ בָּרְחֹבוֹת. שֶׁלֹּא־יִתָּשֵׁל חֶבֶל הַכֶּסֶף וְתִשָּׁבֵר כּוֹס הַזָּהָב, וְתִשָּׁבֵר הַדַּלְיָה בְּהַמָּקוֹר, וְנֶגֶל בְּבֹר יִשָּׁבֵר. וְהָעָפָר יָשׁוּב אֶל־הָאֲדָמָה כַּאֲשֶׁר הָיָה, וְהָרוּחַ תָּשׁוּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר נָתַןָּהּ.” (Ecclesiastes 12:1-7)

\n

בפסקה הזו, התיאור הפואטי נראה שמדבר על אובדן שיניים, אובדן שמיעה, הליכה לא יציבה וחולשה כללית. קשה לומר אם אחת התמונות הללו מתייחסת לאובדן זיכרון. מה שבטוח הוא שהפסוק מתחיל בציווי: “זכור!”

\n

זה לא המקום היחיד בכתובים שבו האדם מצווה לזכור. שוב ושוב נאמר לנו לזכור את האל. עלינו לוודא שאנו מלמדים את ילדינו עליו. “וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ, וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ, וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ, וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ.” (Deuteronomy 6:7)

\n

עלול להגיע זמן שבו לא נוכל לזכור יותר. הדבר החשוב ביותר — גם כשחושבים על נושא הדמנציה — הוא שנזכור את בוראנו ונתעקש ללכת אחריו בכל לבנו.

\n

מהי דמנציה

\n

דמנציה היא כל מחלה שגורמת לאובדן זיכרון, לשיבוש השיפוט ולפגיעה בתפקוד החברתי. רוב האנשים חושבים בעיקר על אובדן הזיכרון. אני מניח שזה מפני שבראשית המחלה אחרים שמים לב לדברים כמו קושי למצוא מילים וחזרה תכופה על סיפורים.

\n

התפקוד החברתי בדרך כלל נשמר עד שלבים מאוחרים במחלה. אם תשאלו מישהו עם דמנציה קלה אם הוא יודע מה התאריך היום, הוא כנראה יענה: “אה, אתה יודע, הפסיקתי לשים לב לדברים כאלה כשיצאתי לפנסיה.”

\n

הגורם השכיח ביותר לדמנציה הוא דמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר — לפחות 70 אחוזים מהאנשים עם אובדן זיכרון מתקדם סובלים מדמנציה של אלצהיימר. נראה שאלצהיימר קשור לחלבונים הנקראים עמילואיד, שמצטברים במוח ומונעים מתאי העצב לתקשר זה עם זה.

\n

גורמים אחרים הם דמנציה וסקולרית, שבה חסימות בכלי הדם במוח גורמות למות תאי עצב. דמנציה מסוג לוי־בודי היא סוג של אובדן זיכרון המלווה במחלת פרקינסון. בערך שמונים אחוזים מהאנשים עם מחלת פרקינסון יפתחו בסופו של דבר דמנציה.

\n

אבחון דמנציה

\n

אם בני משפחה חושדים שמישהו מפתח אובדן זיכרון, הדבר הטוב ביותר הוא להביא אותו לרופא המשפחה להערכה. לצד בדיקה גופנית, הרופא בדרך כלל יבקש מן המטופל לצייר שעון ולעבור מבחן מנטלי קצר, שבו נשאלים הרבה שאלות פשוטות ומבוצעת בדיקת זיכרון קצר־טווח לפריטים.

\n

יבוצעו בדיקות דם כולל תפקוד בלוטת התריס ורמת ויטמין B12. גם סריקת מוח או בדיקת אולטרסאונד לעורקי הצוואר עשויות להיעשות.

\n

המטרה היא לזהות גורמים שאפשר לטפל בהם ולטפל באלה.

\n

הפסקת תרופות

\n \n

תרופות רבות מעלות את הסיכון לבעיות זיכרון. ככל שאנשים מתבגרים, הימנעות מתרופות כאלה מסייעת במניעת התפתחות דמנציה.

\n

תרופות אנטיכולינרגיות הן כנראה האשמות העיקריות שאני נתקל בהן. הנפוצות שבהן הן אנטיהיסטמינים ישנים כמו דיפנהידראמין (משמש כעזר שינה או כדור נגד אלרגיה) ודוקסילאמין (כעזר שינה). במחקר אחד, מטופלים שלקחו תרופה אנטיכולינרגית למשך שקול לשלוש שנים היו בסיכון גבוה משמעותית לפתח דמנציה לעומת מטופלים שלקחו תרופות כאלה פחות משלושה חודשים.1 תרופות ישנות לדיכאון גם עלולות להיכנס לקטגוריה זו.

\n

תרופות לחרדה, הקרויות בנזודיאזפינים, נקשרו גם הן לבעיות זיכרון. מחקרים מצביעים על כך שמטופלים שלוקחים תרופות אלה בסיכון גבוה יותר לפתח דמנציה מאשר מטופלים שאינם נוטלים אותן.2

\n

תרופות נגד פרכוסים עשויות גם להרע את יכולת החשיבה. קיום הפרעה של פרכוסים נראה כמעלה את הסיכון לדמנציה, אך תרופות ישנות מסוימות כמו ולפרואט וגאבפנטין נראות כמקשות על חשיבתם הברורה של אנשים מבוגרים, ולכן במידת האפשר כדאי לעבור לתרופות נגד פרכוסים עם סיכון נמוך יותר לאנשים מבוגרים.

\n

יש מצבים שבהם מישהו צריך לקחת תרופה, אך ככל שהמטופלים מתבגרים חשוב לשקול את הסיכונים של אותן תרופות. קיימת רשימה של תרופות שמומלץ להימנע מהן למטופלים מעל גיל 65, הנקראת רשימת בירס (Beers List). מומלץ להחליף בתרופות דומות עם פחות תופעות לוואי או להשתמש במינונים נמוכים יותר.3

\n

טיפולים רפואיים

\n

הכלל הראשון בטיפול בדמנציה הוא לוודא שכל הדברים המטבוליים בשליטה הטובה ביותר שניתן. כך, אם למישהו יש סוכרת, עדיף לוודא שהסוכר בשליטה הטובה ביותר. אם למישהו לחץ דם גבוה, יש לוודא שהוא מאוזן היטב (זה נכון במיוחד במקרה של דמנציה וסקולרית).

\n

יש כמה קבוצות של תרופות שאושרו לטיפול בדמנציה. קבוצה אחת היא מעכבי כולינוסטראז. תרופות אלה מעלות את רמתו של כימיקל הנקרא אצטילכולין במוח ובמערכת העצבים ההיקפית. תרופות אלה ממש לא תרופות פלא, ולרוב הן נראות כמאיטות את ההתקדמות של אובדן הזיכרון ולא ממש משקמות את תפקוד המוח הקודם.

\n

התרופה השנייה נקראת ממנטין. היא פועלת על קולטני הגלוטמט במוח. כמו במעכבי הכולינוסטראז, ההשפעות אינן אדירות והתוצאה הסופית רק מאטה את אובדן הזיכרון.

\n

שתיהן תרופות גנריות, וסביר לנסותן ולראות כיצד המטופל מגיב.

\n

תרופה אחרונה שראוי להזכיר היא לקאנמאב (lecanemab). מדובר בהזלפה תוך־ורידית שמכוונת לעמילואיד, סוג של חלבון שמצטבר במוח של חולי דמנציה של אלצהיימר. התרופה נראית עובדת היטב בניקוי עמילואיד ממוחות המטופלים. התרופה יקרה מאוד (26,500 דולר בשנה) והיא נקשרה לעלייה בשיעור השבצים. במחקרים תסמיני הדמנציה הוקדמו רק בכ־30 אחוזים ביחס לפלצבו.

\n

לא קיימות כיום תרופות אחרות שאושרו לטיפול בדמנציה.

\n

טיפולים לא תרופתיים

\n

יש כמה דברים שאנשים יכולים לעשות כדי לסייע להאטת התקדמות הדמנציה. אלה יכולים לעזור לאנשים שיש להם היסטוריה משפחתית חזקה של דמנציה ורוצים למנוע את הופעתה.

\n

פעילות אירובית חשובה מאוד. רופאים מזכירים פעילות גופנית בקשר כמעט לכל מחלה כרונית כי הוכח שהיא עובדת. במקרה של דמנציה, אנשים שמתאמנים באופן קבוע מפחיתים בכ־30 אחוז את הסיכון לפתח את המחלה. פעילות סדירה נראית כמאטה את התקדמות הדמנציה.4

\n

פתירת חידות הדורשות פעילות מנטלית, כמו סודוקו או תשחצים, נראית מסייעת להאטת התדרדרות הזיכרון ועשויה גם להפחית את הסיכוי לפתח דמנציה.

\n

ולבסוף, מועיל ללמוד משהו חדש. אנשים שלומדים מיומנות חדשה או מתמקדים בלמידת שפה חדשה מעודדים את הזיכרון שלהם במידה משמעותית. מחקר השווה אנשים מבוגרים שלמדו מיומנות חדשה לאנשים שהלכו לאירועים חברתיים מצא אבחנה מעניינת.

\n

הנקודה נראית להיות שהמוחות שלנו צריכים דחיפה ליצירת דרכים חדשות, אחרת הם נוטים להתפרק.5

\n

טיפול במי שסובל מדמנציה

\n

טיפול במי שסובל מדמנציה מאתגר בכמה מובנים. לעיתים קשה לדעת עד כמה לתת לאדם לשמור על עצמאות. נכתבו ספרים רבים בנושא, אבל יש כמה דברים שכדאי להזכיר.

\n

חשוב להרחיק סכנות. שני הדברים המסוכנים ביותר לאדם עם זיכרון לקוי הם נהיגה ובישול. שניהם נראים שגרתיים, והאדם עלול להיראות במצב תקין, אבל הם יכולים להפוך לבעיה במהירות.

\n

הסכנה של נהיגה ברכב או עגלה היא דו־כיוונית. ראשית, חלק מהאנשים קופאים בנקודות מסוימות, לא זוכרים איך לבצע מיומנות מסוימת. זה יכול להיות מסוכן לא רק עבורם אלא גם עבור אחרים בכביש.

\n

שנית, אנשים מבוגרים יכולים לצאת לנסיעות קצרות לחנות מקומית או למסעדה ולבסוף ללכת לאיבוד. היו לי מטופלים שסיבבו שעות בניסיון למצוא את דרכם הביתה כשרחשים לאיבוד בכביש לעיר.

\n

בישול, כמובן, בסופו של דבר נוגע בזיכרון להניח טיימרים ולהוריד דברים מהכירה או מהתנור בזמן המתאים.

\n

לעיתים קרובות אנשים עם דמנציה אינם מבינים עד כמה יכולותיהם פחתו ומתנגדים להצורך לוותר על המפתחות. אולי זה פשוט קשור לאובדן עצמאות, אבל קשה להתמודד עם העובדה שאינך בטוח מאחורי ההגה.

\n

נסו להשאיר את הדברים זהים בחדר ובבית. אפילו שינויים קטנים בסידור החדר עלולים להספיק כדי להפריע למצב. הוצאת מישהו מביתו — למשל קבלתו לבית חולים — לעיתים קרובות מחמירה את המצב. לפתע, בלבול שנראה קל קודם לכן משתנה לבלבול חמור מאוד.

\n

אם יש פרי של רוח הקודש שחשוב בטיפול במי שסובל מדמנציה, זה הסבלנות. אף אחד מאיתנו לא מחזיק בכמות הסבלנות הנדרשת, וככל שהדמנציה מתקדמת הסבלנות שלנו נשחקת מאוד.

\n

אנשים עם דמנציה מתנהגים לעתים כמו ילדים בנסיעה ארוכה. הם שואלים שוב ושוב מתי חוזרים הביתה. הם תוהים היכן קרובי משפחה שנפטרו או מדוע הילדים עוד לא הגיעו הביתה. שום הסבר לא עוזר, כי דקה או שתיים אחר כך הם שכחו את התשובה ושואלים שוב.

\n

היכולות שלהם לעתים מתעצמות ונחלשות לסירוגין. יום אחד הם מסוגלים לכפתר את החולצה, וביום הבא המיומנות נראית כאילו עפה אל החוץ. קל להאמין שהם לא \"מנסים מספיק\" ושאם רק ינסו יותר היו יכולים לעשות יותר.

\n

לצערנו, העובדה שמישהו עם דמנציה יכל לעשות משהו אתמול אינה מבטיחה שהוא זוכר איך לעשות זאת היום. לכעוס עליהם רק מחמיר את הדברים כי זה מוסיף חרדה לאדם שכבר חסר לו הזיכרון של איך לבצע מיומנות.

\n

ככל שניתן, השיבו לאדם בעדינות גם אם זה הפעם השלושים ושלוש שאתם עונים על אותה שאלה. השתמשו גם בהסחות דעת. אם יש פעילות שהם עדיין יכולים לבצע, כמו תפירה או פאזל (אפילו פאזלים לילדים עם חלקים גדולים מאוד), בקשו מהם לעסוק בה. בשלבים מאוחרים של המחלה, לתת להם להסתכל בספרים עם תמונות יפות או לפעמים אפילו לתת להם בובת תינוק להחזיק יכול לסייע להרגיע ולהסיח אותם מרגעי החרדה שלהם.

\n

השיגו עזרה מאחרים

\n

קל להתוסכל. ניסיון לספק את כל הטיפול בעצמך אינו פתרון לטווח ארוך. הטיפול בדמנציה הוא מרתון ולא ספרינט. רבים חיים שנים לאחר האבחנה, ואף על פי שלגופם הפיזי נותרות לעתים חוסן יחסי, הם זקוקים ליותר ויותר טיפול.

\n

אחת הברכות שבהן יש לקשרים משפחתיים ולקהילות הכנסייה היא שיש לנו אנשים זמינים להושיט יד ולסייע.

\n

שיתוף בני משפחה או חברים שיוכלו להחליף אותך ולתת לך הפסקה הוא המפתח כדי שלא תשחוק או תזדעזע עד כדי כעס כלפי אדם שאתה דואג לו. עדיף לקחת זמן מחוץ מדי פעם לפני שתהיה מותש נפשית. אולי נדמה לך שהכל בסדר, אבל כולנו נוטים להיחלש בעשיית הטוב אם לא מקבלים הפסקה.

\n

סיכום

\n

הלוואי היו יותר פתרונות רפואיים לדמנציה. אולי בעתיד יגיעו עוד. לעת עתה, התרופות מוגבלות למדי.

\n

העיקר הוא ליישם את פרי הרוח. “וּפְרִי הָרוּחַ הוּא־אַהֲבָה, שִׂמְחָה, שָׁלוֹם, אֶרֶךְ אַנְשַׁיִם, טוֹבִים, חֶסֶד, אֱמוּנָה, עֲנָוָה, כְּשָׁרוֹן; עַל־כֵּן אֵין תּוֹרָה.” (Galatians 5:22-23)

\n

גם בימים המתסכלים ביותר, אנשים המתמודדים עם אובדן זיכרון חמור זקוקים לאהבה, ענווה וסבלנות מבני משפחתם. רק בכוח רוח הקודש נוכל להעניק את הטיפול הנדרש למישהו שגופו חזק, אך שכבר לא מזהה אותך אפילו.

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

Mi sembra incredibile vedere come Dio usi il Suo popolo nel corso della storia per rendere gloria al Suo nome. Egli usa le cose deboli per confondere i saggi; le cose umili per ridurre a nulla la sapienza degli uomini mondani. Dio usa la debolezza fisica, le sofferenze, la perdita, il dolore, il lavoro e il patimento per aumentare i nostri tesori spirituali e edificare il Suo Regno qui sulla terra!

Questo inno divenne prezioso per la mia famiglia e per me diversi anni fa, mentre attendevamo la nascita della nostra quarta bambina con difficoltà genetiche. Sapevamo che non sarebbe rimasta con noi a lungo. Morì quando aveva appena tre giorni. Dopo aver ricercato la storia di questo inno, rimasi stupito nello scoprire che l’uomo la cui vita aveva ispirato questo canto aveva perso otto dei suoi nove figli.

La storia di quest’uomo è notevole. I suoi 61 anni su questa terra furono segnati da dolore e perdita, persecuzione e prigionia. Eppure, la sua dedizione a Cristo fu straordinaria, e il suo zelo per Dio e per la predicazione del vangelo non venne meno fino all’ultimo giorno.

Samuel Rutherford, figlio di un contadino benestante, nacque nell’anno 1600. La sua vita ebbe inizio nel piccolo villaggio di Nisbet, in Scozia. Facendo uno sguardo sulla sua vita, notiamo la mano di Dio all’opera negli anni dell’infanzia di Samuel. A soli tre anni stava giocando con i suoi amici quando cadde nel pozzo del paese. Sua sorella e gli amici corsero a chiedere aiuto. Quando ritornarono, trovarono un Samuel molto fradicio seduto sull’erba accanto al pozzo. Gli chiesero come fosse uscito, e lui rispose: "Un bel uomo vestito di bianco venne e mi tirò fuori dal pozzo." La sua famiglia credette che Dio avesse mandato un angelo a salvarlo quel giorno.

Da quanto sappiamo di Samuel Rutherford, aveva due fratelli e una sorella. Fu mandato a scuola da piccolo e divenne uno studente molto diligente. Imparò così bene il latino e il greco che divenne in seguito professore. Sposò Eupham Hamilton intorno al 1624, poco dopo aver iniziato a insegnare all’Università di Edimburgo. A quel tempo Samuel non era ancora convertito e si preoccupava soltanto di perseguire i suoi obiettivi accademici.

Nel 1626, all’età di 26 anni, Samuel giunse a una fede chiara e salvifica nel Signore Gesù Cristo. Egli disse: "O ma Cristo ha un occhio salvifico. Quando Egli per la prima volta posò lo sguardo su di me, fui salvato. Gli costò soltanto uno sguardo per rendere l’inferno inutile per me." Da quel momento fu pieno di passione per predicare e parlare del suo Salvatore. Questo cambiamento di vita causò tale scalpore nell’università che Rutherford finì per dimettersi dalla cattedra.

Nel 1627 Samuel portò sua moglie e i due figli piccoli a Galloway, in Scozia, dove iniziò a pastoreggiare la piccola chiesa di Anwoth. Nel cominciare il suo ministero disse: "Ho ricevuto la commissione dal Reale e Principesco Maestro, il mio Signore Gesù, di predicare Cristo al popolo." La sua passione era la conversione della gente, e si dice che sembrasse sempre pregare, sempre predicare, sempre visitare gli ammalati, sempre insegnare e istruire, sempre scrivere o studiare. Il zelo con cui predicava e la sua cura per il benessere della sua congregazione ebbero grande effetto su di loro. Non solo loro: persone venivano dai paesi e villaggi circostanti per ascoltare la sua predicazione. Un amico riferì una volta: "Molte volte ho pensato che sarebbe volato fuori dal pulpito quando veniva a parlare di Gesù Cristo."

Samuel non fu estraneo al dolore e al cordoglio. Nel 1631, soltanto quattro anni dopo aver iniziato il suo lavoro come pastore, sua moglie morì. Anche i suoi due figli si ammalarono e uscirono da questo mondo. Nel 1636, dopo nove anni di predicazione, fu esiliato ad Aberdeen, dove gli fu proibito di predicare il vangelo. Questo fu un periodo molto difficile per lui, poiché gli mancavano profondamente la moglie, i figli e la sua congregazione, la Chiesa di Anwoth. Questo periodo della sua vita è infatti uno dei motivi per cui è così ricordato, perché iniziò a scrivere lettere alla sua gente di chiesa e agli amici. Delle 365 lettere che scrisse, 220 furono redatte durante questi 22 mesi di esilio.

Il governo alla fine cambiò, il che diede maggiore libertà ai dissenzienti Covenanter. Di conseguenza Rutherford tornò rapidamente al suo amato gregge di Anwoth. Circa un anno dopo, nell’autunno del 1639, lasciò di nuovo Anwoth di malavoglia, ma questa volta per assumere l’incarico di Professore di Divinità al St Mary's College di St. Andrews. Questo cambiamento fu difficile per lui, poiché di nuovo sentiva moltissimo la mancanza della sua congregazione. Scrive: "Il mio allontanamento dal mio gregge è per me così grave, che rende la mia vita un peso; non ebbi mai tanto desiderio di morire. Il Signore aiuti e sostenga questa triste argilla."

Dopo cinque mesi nella sua nuova posizione e dopo essere stato quasi dieci anni da solo, il quarantenne Samuel sposò Jean McMath. Insieme ebbero sette figli. Purtroppo, sei di loro morirono in tenera età e nell’infanzia. Solo una figlia di nome Agnes sopravvisse fino all’età adulta.

Rutherford continuò a essere un leader influente nel movimento nonconformista in Scozia per i successivi 20 anni fino al 1660. Con la morte di Cromwell, il governo del Commonwealth ebbe fine e Carlo II fu restaurato al potere. Ancora una volta, l’ira della monarchia si abbatté su Samuel. Fu convocato davanti al giudice e accusato di alto tradimento contro il governo per aver predicato la verità. Fu messo in prigione in attesa di esecuzione. Tuttavia, prima che il re potesse condannarlo a morte, Samuel si ammalò gravemente. Egli disse: "Ho già una citazione da un Giudice superiore, e devo rispondere alla mia prima citazione e quando verrà il vostro giorno io sarò dove pochi re e persone grandi vengono."

Tardi nel pomeriggio dell’ultimo giorno della sua vita, in risposta alla domanda: "Che pensate ora di Cristo?" rispose così: "Oh, che tutti i miei fratelli nella terra possano sapere che Maestro ho servito, e quale pace ho oggi! Dormirò in Cristo, e quando mi risveglierò sarò soddisfatto della Sua somiglianza. Questa notte chiuderà la porta, e poserà la mia ancora entro il velo, e me ne andrò in un sonno verso le cinque del mattino. Gloria! gloria al mio Creatore e mio Redentore in eterno! Vivrò e Lo adorerò. Oh, per braccia che Lo abbraccino! Oh, per un'arpa ben accordata! Gloria! la gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel!" Queste parole furono udite da sua moglie, dalla figlia e dagli amici, e egli fu davvero con il suo Signore alle cinque del mattino.

Quasi due secoli dopo, Annie Ross Cousin, poetessa e autrice di inni scozzese e moglie di un ministro, fu ispirata dalla vita e dagli scritti di Samuel Rutherford. Riassunse la sua vita in un inno biografico, "The Sands of Time are Sinking". Questo inno fu pubblicato per la prima volta nel 1857 nel Christian Treasury. Delle diciannove strofe originali, soltanto quattro sono utilizzate nei nostri libri di inni. (in copia in grassetto)

Le sabbie del tempo stanno affondando,
L’alba del cielo si spezza,
Il mattino estivo che ho sospirato,
Il bel, dolce mattino si desta:
Buia, buia è stata la mezzanotte,
Ma l’aurora è a portata di mano,
E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel.

2. Oh! bene è per sempre,
Oh! bene per sempre ancora:
il mio nido non posa in alcuna foresta
di questa riva destinata alla morte!
Sì, lasciate che il vano mondo svanisca,
Come dal ponte della nave,
Mentre E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel.

3. Lì la Rosa Rossa di Sharon
Schiude il suo cuore più profondo.
E riempie l’aria del Cielo
Con un profumo inebriante;
Oh, poter contemplare il suo fiore,
Mentre dalla sua fragranza ventilato
Dove E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel.

4. Il Re là nella Sua bellezza,
Senza velo è visto:
Sarebbe un viaggio ben speso
Anche se sette morti stessero tra mezzo:
L’Agnello con il Suo bello esercito,
Sta sul Monte Sion;
E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel.

5. Oh! Cristo Egli è la fonte,
Il profondo dolce pozzo d’Amore!
I ruscelli sulla terra che ho gustato,
Più profondamente berrò sopra;
Là, fino alla pienezza oceanica,
La Sua misericordia si espande,
E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel.

6. Perfino Anwoth non era il cielo—
Perfino la predicazione non era Cristo;
E nella mia prigione battuta dal mare
Il mio Signore e io avemmo un appuntamento:
E sempre la mia nube di tempesta più oscura
Fu da un arcobaleno distesa,
Catturata dalla gloria che dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

7. Ma che Egli costruì un cielo
Del Suo amore eccedente,
Una piccola Nuova Gerusalemme,
Simile a quella lassù,—
“Signore, portami oltre l’acqua,”
Sarebbe stata la mia alta richiesta,
“Portami nel paese dell’amore,
Verso la terra di Immanuel.”

8. Ma i fiori hanno bisogno del fresco buio della notte,
Della luce della luna e della rugiada;
Così Cristo, da chi lo amava,
Il Suo splendore spesso ritirò;
E allora, a cagione dell’assenza,
Esaminavo la mia anima turbata—
Ma la gloria, senza ombra, risplende
Nella terra di Immanuel.

9. I piccoli uccelli di Anwoth,
si diceva fossero benedetti,—
Ora, accanto ad altari più felici,
vanno a costruire il mio nido:
Su questi non aleggia silenzio,
Non ci sono tombe intorno a loro,
Perché gloria, immortale, dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

10. Bella Anwoth sul Solway,
Per me tu resti cara!
Perfino dal ciglio del Cielo
Io verso di te lascio una lacrima.
Oh! se un’anima di Anwoth
Mi incontrasse alla destra di Dio,
Il mio Cielo sarà due Cieli,
Nella terra di Immanuel!

11. Ho lottato verso il Cielo,
Contro tempesta, vento e marea;—
Ora, come un viaggiatore stanco,
Che si appoggia alla sua guida,
Tra le ombre della sera,
Mentre affonda la sabbia che indugia la vita,
Saluto l’apparire della gloria
Dalla terra di Immanuel.

12. Acque profonde hanno attraversato il sentiero della vita,
La siepe di spine era acuta;
Ora queste sono tutte dietro di me,—
Oh, per un’arpa ben accordata!
Oh, unirsi all’Aleluia
Con quella banda trionfante,
Che cantano dove la gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel!

13. Con misericordia e con giudizio
La mia tela del tempo Egli tessé,
E sempre le rugiade del dolore
Furono illuminate dal Suo amore!
Benedico la mano che guidò,
Benedico il cuore che progettò,
Quando assetato dove la gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

14. Presto la coppa della gloria
Laverà i più amari affanni della terra,
Presto la spina del deserto
Fiorirà nella rosa dell’Eden:
La maledizione muterà in benedizione–
Il nome sulla terra che è bandito,
Sarà inciso sulla pietra bianca
Nella terra di Immanuel.

15. Oh! Io sono della mia Diletta,
E la mia Diletta è mia!
Porta un povero miserabile peccatore
Nella Sua “casa del vino”:
Io sto sul Suo merito,
Non conosco altra base,
Neppure dove la gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

16. Dormirò profondamente in Gesù,
Ricolmo della Sua somiglianza sorgerò,
Per vivere e per adorarLo,
Per vederLo con questi occhi:
Tra me e la risurrezione
Ma il Paradiso sta;
Allora—allora per dimorare nella gloria
Nella terra di Immanuel!

17. La sposa non guarda il suo vestito,
Ma il volto del suo caro Sposo;
Io non contemplerò la gloria,
Ma il mio Re di Grazia—
Non alla corona che Egli dona,
Ma alla Sua mano trafitta:
L’Agnello è tutta la gloria
Della terra di Immanuel.

18. Ho sopportato disprezzo e odio,
Ho sopportato torto e vergogna,
I superbi della terra mi hanno rimproverato,
Per il triplice benedetto nome di Cristo:
Dove Dio pose il Suo sigillo più bello
Loro hanno impresso il loro marchio più infame;
Ma il giudizio splende come mezzogiorno
Nella terra di Immanuel.

19. Mi hanno convocato davanti a loro,
Ma là io non posso venire,—
Il mio Signore dice, "Salite quassù",
Il mio Signore dice, "Benvenuto a casa!
Il mio Re ora al Suo trono bianco,
Comanda la mia presenza,
Dove E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel.

La bella melodia complementare per questo testo fu composta nei primi anni del 1800 da un musicista francese, Chretien D`Urhan. Si adatta bene alle parole dell’inno—il suo tempo solenne corrisponde alla solennità delle parole. La linea melodica ascendente dell’ultima frase si accorda perfettamente con la gioia attesa espressa dal ritornello—"E gloria — gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel."

Concludendo questa storia dell’inno, continuiamo a stupirci della provvidenza di Dio nelle vite di coloro che ci hanno preceduto. Seguiamo Cristo con tutto il cuore ed essere vasi pronti all’uso del Maestro! Un’ultima citazione di Samuel Rutherford da portarci dietro. "Non perdono nulla coloro che acquistano Cristo."

Le informazioni per questo articolo sono state tratte da 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.

It's incredible to me to see how God uses His people throughout history to bring glory to His name. He uses the weak things to confound the wise; the base things to bring to nothing the wisdom of earthly wise men. God uses physical weakness, hardship, loss, grief, toil, and pain to increase our spiritual treasures and build His Kingdom here on the earth!

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

من المدهش بالنسبة لي أن أرى كيف يستخدم الله شعبه عبر التاريخ ليُعظّم اسمه. إنه يستخدم الأشياء الضعيفة ليُحير الحكماء؛ والأشياء الدنيئة ليبطل حكمة الحكماء الأرضيين. يستعمل الله الضعف الجسدي، والمشقة، والفقدان، والحزن، والكَدّ، والألم لزيادة كنوزنا الروحية وبناء ملكوته هنا على الأرض!

صارت هذه المرتلة ثمينة لعائلتي ولي قبل عدة سنوات بينما كنا ننتظر ولادة طفلنا الرابع الذي يعاني من عيب جيني. كنا نعلم أنها لن تبقى معنا طويلاً. فقدت حياتها بعد ثلاثة أيام فقط من ولادتها. بعد أن بحثت في تاريخ هذه المرتلة، دهشت عندما اكتشفت أن الرجل الذي كانت قصته مصدر إلهام هذه المرتلة قد فقد ثمانية من أصل تسعة من أولاده.

قصة هذا الرجل جديرة بالملاحظة. استُغرقت سنواته الـ61 على هذه الأرض بالحزن والخسارة والاضطهاد والسجن. ومع ذلك، كانت تفانيه للمسيح بارزاً، ولم يخفت حماسه تجاه الله وحرصه على تبشير الإنجيل حتى يومه الأخير.

وُلد صموئيل رذرفورد، ابن فلاح مزدهر، في سنة 1600. بدأت حياته في قرية صغيرة اسمها نيسبت في اسكتلندا. عندما نلمح حياته نلاحظ عمل يد الله في سنواته الأولى. إذ كان في الثالثة من عمره يلعب مع أصدقائه ثم سقط في بئر البلدة. ركضت أخته وأصدقاؤه لطلب المساعدة. عندما عادوا وجدوا صموئيل مبللاً جداً جالساً على العشب بجانب البئر. سألوا كيف خرج، فأجاب: "رجل أبيض جميل جاء وأخرجني من البئر." آمنت أسرته أن الله أرسل ملاكاً لإنقاذه ذلك اليوم.

مما نعرفه عن صموئيل رذرفورد أنه كان له أخوان وأخت واحدة. أُرسل إلى المدرسة وهو صغير، فأصبح طالباً مجتهداً جداً. تعلَّم اللاتينية واليونانية جيداً إلى درجة أنه أصبح في النهاية أستاذاً. تزوَّج إبفام هاملتون حوالي عام 1624، بعد وقت قصير من بدء عمله التدريسي في جامعة إدنبرة. في ذلك الوقت، لم يكن صموئيل قد تَحوّل بعد، ولم يهتم إلا بمتابعة أهدافه الأكاديمية.

في عام 1626، وفي سن السادسة والعشرين، جاء صموئيل إلى إيمان واضح وخلاص في الرب يسوع المسيح. قال: "أوه، إن المسيح له عين خلاص. عندما نظر إليّ أول مرة خُليتُ. لم يكلفه إلا نظرة ليجعل الجحيم يفر مني." من تلك اللحظة امتلأ بشغف للوعظ وللحديث عن مخلصه. تسبب هذا التغيير في حياته في إثارة كبيرة في الجامعة حتى استقال رذرفورد من أستاذيته.

في عام 1627، أخذ صموئيل زوجته وطفليه الصغيرين إلى غالواي في اسكتلندا، حيث بدأ رعاية كنيسة أنووث الصغيرة. عندما بدأ دعوته هناك قال: "لقد تلقيت التكليف من السيد الملكي والأمير، سيدي يسوع، أن أكرز بالمسيح للشعب." كان شغفه هو هداية الناس، ويُقال إنه كان يبدو دائماً كأنه يصلي، دائماً يوعظ، دائماً يزور المرضى، دائماً يُعلّم ويُرشد، دائماً يكتب أو يدرس. كان الحماس الذي وعظ به واهتمامه برفاهية رعيته له أثر عظيم عليهم. لم يأتِ المستمعون فقط من قريته، بل جاء الناس من البلدات والقرى المحيطة لسماع وعظه. وروى صديق مرة: "كثيراً ما ظننت أنه كان سيطير من فوق المنبر عندما يتكلم عن يسوع المسيح."

لم يَغب الحزن والأسى عن حياة صموئيل. ففي عام 1631، بعد أربع سنوات فقط من بدء عمله كراعي، توفيت زوجته. كما مرض طفلاه وغادرا هذه الدنيا. في عام 1636، وبعد تسع سنوات من الوعظ، نُفي إلى أبردين، حيث مُنع من تبشير الإنجيل. كانت هذه فترة صعبة عليه إذ اشتاق كثيراً إلى زوجته وأطفاله وإلى رعيته، كنيسة أنووث. وهذه الفترة في حياته هي بالفعل سبب من أسباب تذكره، لأنه بدأ يكتب رسائل إلى شعب كنيسته وأصدقائه. من بين 365 رسالة كتبها، كُتبت 220 رسالة خلال 22 شهراً من النفي.

تغيرت الحكومة في نهاية المطاف، مما منح مزيداً من الحرية لرفقاء العهد غير المهادين. فعاد رذرفورد سريعاً إلى رعيته المحبوبة في أنووث. بعد نحو عام، في خريف 1639، غادر أنووث مرة أخرى على مضض لكن هذه المرة لتلبية تعيين ليصبح أستاذاً لللاهوت في كلية القديسة ماريز في سانت أندروز. كان هذا التغيير صعباً عليه، إذ اشتاق مجدداً إلى رعيته. يكتب: "نقلي عن رعيتي ثقيل عليّ جداً، حتى جعَل حياتي عبئاً عليّ، لم أحظَ يوماً بمثل هذا الشوق للموت. ليعينني الرب ويحفظ هذا الطين الحزين."

بعد خمسة أشهر في منصبه الجديد وبعد أن عاش وحيداً لما يقرب من عشر سنوات، تزوج صموئيل، البالغ من العمر أربعين سنة، من جين مكماث. أنجبا معاً سبعة أطفال. للأسف، مات ستة منهم في فترة الرضاعة والطفولة المبكرة. لم تبقَ سوى ابنة تُدعى أغنس نمت حتى البلوغ.

استمر رذرفورد قائداً مؤثراً في الحركة غير المهادية في اسكتلندا للعشرين سنة التالية حتى عام 1660. مع وفاة كرومويل، انتهى حكم الكومنولث، واستعاد تشارلز الثاني السلطة. وسقطت مرة أخرى غضبة الملكية على صموئيل. استُدعي ليظهر أمام القضاة وُوجه بتهمة الخيانة العظمى ضد الحكومة بسبب تبشيره بالحق. حُوّل إلى السجن انتظاراً لإعدامه. ومع ذلك، قبل أن يمكّن الملك من إعدامه، مرض صموئيل مرضاً شديداً. قال: "لديّ استدعاء بالفعل من قاضٍ أرفع، ويجب أن أجيب على استدعائي الأول، وعندما يحين يومكم سأكون حيث قليل من الملوك والأشخاص العظام يأتون."

في فترة متأخرة من بعد ظهر آخر يوم في حياته، وفي إجابة على سؤال "ما رأيكم الآن بالمسيح؟" أجاب هكذا: "يا ليت جميع إخوتي في الأرض يعرفون أي سيد قد خدمت، وأي سلام أملكه هذا اليوم! سأنام في المسيح، وعندما أقوم سأُشبع بشبهه. هذه الليلة ستغلق الباب، وتثبت مراسي داخل الحجاب، وسأرحل في نوم عند الخامسة من الصباح. المجد! المجد للخالق والمخلص إلى الأبد! سأحيا وأعبده. يا ليت لي أذانٌ لأحضنه! يا ليت لي قيثارةٌ مضبوطة النغم! المجد! المجد يسكن في أرض عمانوئيل!" سمعت هذه الكلمات زوجته وابنته وأصدقاؤه، وكان بالفعل مع ربه عند الخامسة صباحاً.

بعد ما يقرب من قرنين، ألهمت آنّي روس كوزين، شاعرة ومؤلفة أنشودة اسكتلندية وزوجة قس، بحياة وكتابات صموئيل رذرفورد. لخّصت حياته في أنشودة سيرة ذاتية بعنوان "حبات الرمل ترقُد". نُشرت هذه الأنشودة لأول مرة عام 1857 في Christian Treasury. من بين تسعة عشر بيتاً أصلياً، يُستخدم فقط أربعة في كتب ترانيمنا. (بنص عريض)

حبات الرمل ترقُد،
فجر السماء يشرق،
الصباح الصيفي الذي ظننتُه،
الصباح الجميل الحنون يستيقظ:
كان الليل مظلماً مظلماً،
لكن صبح الآيام قريب،
والمجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

2. آه! حسنٌ هو إلى الأبد،
آه! حسنٌ إلى الأبد
عشِّي لم يكن مُعلّقاً
في أي غابة من هذا الشاطئ المحكوم بالموت!
نعم، دع العالم الباطل يزول،
كما عن المركب الوقوف،
بينما المجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

3. هناك وردة شارون الحمراء
تكشف أزهارها الأعمق قلباً.
وتملأ هواء السماء
بعطر فاتن؛
آه، لأرى تفتحها،
بينما يروّحها عبيرها
حيث المجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

4. الملك هناك في جلاله،
يُرى دون حجاب:
ستكون رحلة جيدة الإنفاق
لو أن سبع موتات بيننا:
الخروف مع جيشه الجميل،
يقف على جبل صهيون؛
والمجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

5. آه! المسيح هو الينبوع،
البئر العميق الحلو للمحبة!
الجداول على الأرض التي ذقْتُها،
سأشرب أعمق فوق؛
هناك، إلى امتلاء محيطي،
تتسع رحمته،
والمجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

6. حتى أنووث لم تكن السماء—
حتى الوعظ لم يكن المسيح؛
وفي سجني المضروب بأمواج البحر
وافقني ربي على الموعد:
ودائماً كان أكثر سحب عاصفي سوادي
يحيط بقوس قزح،
مأخوذة من المجد الساكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

7. لكن أنه بنى سماء
من محبته الفائقة،
أورشليم جديدة صغيرة،
شبيهة بتلك الفوقى,—
"يا رب، خذني عبر الماء،"
كانت طلبي الصاخب،
"خذني إلى بلد المحبة نفسها،
إلى أرض عمانوئيل."

8. لكن الأزهار تحتاج ظلمة الليل الباردة،
ضوء القمر والندى؛
هكذا المسيح، من محبٍ أحبها،
كثيراً ما سحب إشراقه؛
ثم، لسبب الغياب،
كنت أفحص نفسي الروحية المضطربة—
لكن المجد، بلا ظل، يضيء
في أرض عمانوئيل.

9. طيور أنووث الصغيرة،
كنت أعدّهم مبارَكين,—
الآن، بجوار مذابح أسعد،
يذهبون لبناء عشّي:
لا يسود فوقها صمت،
لا قبور تحيط بها،
لأن المجد، الخالد، يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

10. أنووث الجميلة بجانب سولواي،
ما زلتَ عزيزاً عليّ!
حتى من حافة السماء
أسقط من أجلك دمعة.
آه! إن التقى روح واحدة من أنووث بي
عند يمين الله،
فسيكون سمائي سمائين،
في أرض عمانوئيل!

11. لقد كافحت نحو السماء،
ضد العاصفة والرياح والمد والجزر;—
الآن، مثل مسافر مُتَعَب،
يتكئ على مرشده،
بين ظلال المساء،
بينما يغرق رمل الحياة المتمدد،
أحيّي فجر المجد الآتي
من أرض عمانوئيل.

12. عبرت مياه عميقة طريق الحياة،
وسياج الشوك كان حاداً;
الآن كل هذا وراءي,—
آه، ليت لي قيثارةٌ مضبوطة النغم!
أن أشترك في هللويا
مع تلك الفرقة المنتصرة،
الذين يغنون حيث يسكن المجد
في أرض عمانوئيل!

13. بالرحمة وبالحكم
نسج زمني هو،
ودائماً كانت ندى الحزن
متلألئة بمحبتِه!
سأبارك اليد التي هدَت،
سأبارك القلب الذي خطط،
عندما أجلس هناك حيث يسكن المجد
في أرض عمانوئيل.

14. قريباً كأس المجد
سيغسل أليمَ الأرض الأكثر مرارة،
قريباً سيتحول الشوك الصحراوي
إلى وردة عدن:
سيتبدل اللعنة إلى بركة–
الاسم الملعون على الأرض،
سينقش على الحجر الأبيض
في أرض عمانوئيل.

15. آه! أنا للمعشوق لي،
والمعشوق ليّ!
يدخِل خطيئاً وضيّعاً فقيراً
إلى "بيت خمره":
أقف على استحقاقه،
لا أعرف موقفاً آخر،
حتى حيث يسكن المجد
في أرض عمانوئيل.

16. سأنام بسلام في يسوع،
مملوءاً بشبَهِه أقوم،
لأحيا وأعبده،
لأراه بعينيَّ هاتين:
بيني وبين القيامة
لا شيء سوى الفردوس قائماً؛
ثم—ثم للمجد الساكن
في أرض عمانوئيل!

17. العروس لا تبصر ثوبها،
بل وجه عريسها الحبيب؛
لن أحدق بالمجد،
بل في ملكي النِعمة—
لا في التاج الذي يعطيه،
بل في يده المثقوبة:
الخروف هو كل المجد
لأرض عمانوئيل.

18. تحملت الاحتقار والبغض،
تحملت الظلم والعار،
الكبرياء الأرضي قذفني بالسب،
من أجل اسم المسيح المبارك ثلاثاً:
حيث وضع الله ختمه أجملهم
طبعوا عليهم أقذر علاماتهم;
لكن الحكم يشرق كظهيرة يوم
في أرض عمانوئيل.

19. لقد استدعوني أمامهم،
لكن لا أستطيع أن آتي هناك,—
يقول ربي، "تعال إلى هنا،"
يقول ربي، "أهلاً بالوطن!"
ملكي الآن على عرشه الأبيض،
حضوري يأمر،
حيث المجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

اللحن التكميلي الجميل لهذا النص ألّفه موسيقي فرنسي، كريستيان دُرهان، في أوائل القرن التاسع عشر. إنه ملائم تماماً لكلمات الترنيمة—إيقاعه الجاد يوافق جدية الكلمات. الخط اللحني الصاعد في العبارة الأخيرة يطابق تماماً الفرح المنتظر المعبر عنه في المقطع المتكرر—"والمجد، المجد يسكن في أرض عمانوئيل."

بينما نختم تاريخ هذه المرتلة، لنتأمل في عناية الله في حياة الذين سبقونا. لنسلك وراء المسيح بكل قلوبنا ونكن أوانٍ جاهزة لاستخدام السيد! اقتباس أخير لصموئيل رذرفورد لنأخذه معنا: "لا يخسر شيئاً من يكسب المسيح."
